clue.text: Fairy tale starts to unravel, lecherous animal showing a bit of leg

parts.note: a fairy tale is a made-up story, a fib

indicators.note: the starts, or first letters, of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A fairy story falls apart as a randy creature shows off a glimpse of its leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes U, L and A from 'unravel, lecherous, animal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fibula is the outer bone of the lower leg, so it is literally one bit of a leg.

clue.text: Sounds like one number plus another number is a lot

indicators.note: says the two numbers are said aloud and heard as one word

parts.note: four and ten, two numbers placed side by side

explanation.surface: A sum-like riddle: two numbers added together make a large amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four ten' said quickly sounds like the answer; 'plus' only joins the two numbers, it does not add them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune is a large sum of money, a lot in the sense of a great deal.

clue.text: On which a squatter may be counting back two from 6 June 1944, fancifully speaking?

definitions.text: On which a squatter may be

indicators.note: a loose pronunciation is asked for: the letters are said aloud as a word

parts.note: 6 June 1944 is D-Day; go back two letters from D and you reach B, giving B-Day

explanation.surface: A wartime-history puzzle about counting down from the Normandy landings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B-day' said as 'bee-day' is the French way of saying the bathroom fitting. A 'squatter' is not a homeless occupier but someone crouching over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low basin one sits or crouches over for washing, so a squatter may be on it.

clue.text: Learning Gaelic in Latvia? Not entirely!

parts.note: a Lett is a native of Latvia

indicators.note: the Gaelic word is not given whole: its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: A question about whether Gaelic is studied in Latvia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the last letter of the Gaelic word. A Lett is a person, not the country, but the clue loosely lets Latvia stand for its native.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters means learning or scholarship, as in a man of letters.

clue.text: Finished attempt to get result

parts.note: time is up when it is finished
a shot is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: A completed effort produces an outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the final outcome or consequence of something.

clue.text: US author has to hear literary work

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: An American writer has to listen to a piece of literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hear' is in the legal sense of trying a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry is verse, a form of literary composition.

clue.text: US author, another with heartless novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters take a new order
with its middle letters removed, the word with keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An American writer teams up with another to produce a novel lacking heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' reduces 'with' to WH, and 'novel' rearranges WH with ANOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne was the American novelist who wrote The Scarlet Letter.

clue.text: Cook three times, real pastry

indicators.note: to cook something is to alter or fiddle it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so three of them give three Ts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A baking instruction: cook three times to make genuine pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges TTT with REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartlet is a small tart, an individual pastry case with a filling.

clue.text: Turn handles on the rack over King Stephen's head — he's tall and thin!

parts.note: to spin is to turn round

indicators.note: a rack tortures and twists, so the letters are stretched into a new order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the head of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A torturer turns the handles of the rack over King Stephen, who is consequently stretched long and thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rack' rearranges HANDLES into DLESHAN; 'over' just places SPIN first in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Spindleshanks is an old nickname for a person with long, thin legs.

clue.text: Dig right inside capsule

indicators.note: one letter is placed within the other piece

parts.note: a pod is a seed capsule, or a detachable capsule on a spacecraft

explanation.surface: An instruction to excavate with the proper equipment inside a capsule.
explanation.definitionFit: A dig is a poke or jab, the same as a prod.

clue.text: Collective elements of a party elite fighting to infiltrate extremists in tribe

indicators.note: the inner pieces get inside the outer letters, as spies infiltrate a group
the extreme, outermost letters of the word tribe

parts.note: the upper class is the elite
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Members of a party elite go to war to penetrate the fringes of a tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists in tribe' gives T and E. 'party' is not political: it is the home sales party where these plastic containers are sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Tupperware is a brand of plastic food containers famously sold at home parties, a collective term for those items.

clue.text: Supporter of women once in ferment

definitions.meaning: a pad or frame once worn to hold out the back of a woman's skirt
a state of busy commotion and activity

explanation.surface: A historical champion of women's rights in a period of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter of women' suggests a suffragist, but it is a piece of Victorian underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustle was a padded support for skirts, and bustle also means excited activity.

clue.text: Last of shag filling inhaler adapted as smoking pipe

indicators.note: one letter fills a gap inside the other letters
the letters of inhaler are changed into a new arrangement
the final letter of the word shag

explanation.surface: The remnants of some tobacco are stuffed into an inhaler converted into a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges INHALER as NARHILE, and G from 'shag' goes inside. Shag is a strong shredded tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A narghile is an oriental water pipe, the hookah, used for smoking tobacco.

clue.text: Recently married man, outfit in black and white

parts.note: recently made or bought is new
a man is a piece in chess, and the castle or rook is one
a married couple are joined as one, wed

explanation.surface: A newly wed groom in a black and white outfit, perhaps a dinner suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outfit' is a team, not clothing: this football club from north-east England plays in black and white stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: The football club is a team, which can be called an outfit, and its kit is black-and-white stripes.

clue.text: Fish oil as horrid for beef

parts.note: the char is a fish of the trout family

indicators.note: something horrid is unpleasant and rough, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A disgusted complaint that fish oil is as nasty as bad beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrid' rearranges OIL AS into OLAIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Charolais is a French breed of cattle raised for beef.

clue.text: Nip round back of boozer, showing some pace

indicators.note: the drink goes round the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a nip is a small drink of spirits, a tot

indicators.note: the last letter of the word boozer

explanation.surface: Someone nips round the back of the pub, moving fairly quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nip' seems to be a verb of movement but is a small drink. A boozer is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A trot is a gait, one speed of moving between walking and running.

clue.text: Colours fade

definitions.meaning: a regiment's or ship's colours are its banner

explanation.definitionFit: A flag is a banner or colours, and to flag is to tire or weaken.

clue.text: At last, a supporter of the steering mechanism?

parts.note: a fin steers a fish or a rocket
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: Finally, a helper for the steering gear has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads a backer of the fin, i.e. FIN then ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Finally means eventually, after a long time, which is the sense of at last.

clue.text: Is old, old tennis player (about a hundred) descriptive of some figure?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the tennis player's name goes about the letter, around it

parts.note: Monica Seles, the former tennis champion
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A veteran tennis player is described as about a hundred years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C inside SELES.
explanation.definitionFit: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, so the word describes a geometric figure.

clue.text: Shaved round fringes in tonsure, so cut

indicators.note: the shaved word goes round the two letters

parts.note: shorn means shaved or clipped

indicators.note: the fringes are the outer letters of the word tonsure

explanation.surface: A monk's head is shaved around the edges of his tonsure, and so it is trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fringes in tonsure' gives T and E, which SHORN goes 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten something is to cut it down, reducing its length.

clue.text: In conclusion, crack cocaine ultimately taken

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed in the word for conclusion

parts.note: the end is the conclusion
a crack is a joke or gag

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of cocaine

explanation.surface: A drug story: in the end, crack cocaine was finally consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' and 'cocaine' look like one drug, but crack is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat or a person that is engaged is already taken, booked or occupied.

clue.text: If patient, batting is superior

indicators.note: superior means above, so in this down entry it comes first

parts.note: in cricket the batting side is in
a doctor's patient is a case

explanation.surface: A sporting claim that batting is the better choice if one is patient.
explanation.definitionFit: In case means if, as in 'in case it rains' introducing a condition.

clue.text: Trouble resting in mansion, I supposed

indicators.note: supposed in the sense of imagined or not real, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone in a grand house guesses they will have trouble sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supposed' signals that MANSION and I are rearranged; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is the inability to sleep, a difficulty in getting rest.

clue.text: House in the shade

definitions.meaning: a colour, between red and yellow

explanation.surface: A house sitting in the shadow of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Orange is a European royal dynasty, and orange is also a colour.

clue.text: A bit to one side

parts.note: a part is a bit or portion

explanation.surface: A small portion is set aside from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means aside or separate, set off to one side away from others.

clue.text: Where cheap goods sold, scrap metal and fake Rolexes, primarily?

indicators.note: to scrap is to break up, so these letters are broken and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means first, the opening letter of Rolexes

explanation.surface: A market stall selling scrap metal and counterfeit watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like part of 'scrap metal' but signals a rearrangement of METAL, FAKE and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea market is an open-air market for cheap second-hand goods.

clue.text: Mythical vessel written about in biography

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters are read backwards
the letters are found inside the word biography

explanation.surface: A legendary ship features in someone's life story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds OGRA inside 'biography' and 'written about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship Jason and the Argonauts sailed in Greek myth.

clue.text: Country welcoming first of slimy sycophants

indicators.note: the country takes the letter in, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: Yemen, the country in Arabia

indicators.note: the first letter of slimy

explanation.surface: A nation welcomes the leading flatterers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are people who agree with everything a superior says, flatterers and toadies.

clue.text: See 13
